findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "iter0_check_site" stacks urgency/override words (important, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: iter0_get_site_status, iter0_get_design_set_status, iter0_check_site, iter0_get_canvas_feedback, iter0_reply_to_feedback, iter0_read_canvas_page · Private data: iter0_get_developer_docs, iter0_restore_version, iter0_check_site, iter0_publish_site, iter0_push_site · Public sink: iter0_publish_site, iter0_publish_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: iter0_get_site_status, iter0_get_design_set_status, iter0_check_site, iter0_get_canvas_feedback, iter0_reply_to_feedback, iter0_read_canvas_page · Private data: iter0_get_developer_docs, iter0_restore_version, iter0_check_site, iter0_publish_site, iter0_push_site · Public sink: iter0_publish_site, iter0_publish_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
